the vitamin D3 metabolite 1,25-dihydroxy vitamin D3 increases the number of epidermal receptor binding sites in BT-20 cells, and it modifies the intracellular distribution of the internalized epidermal growth factors.
1. 25 dihydroxy-vitamin D3 increases EGF-R level and modifies EGF internalization in BT-20 cells, but it does not modify the time course of EGF internalization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of vitamin D on EGF-R in BT-20 mammary carcinoma cells.
the effects of vitamin D3 on cell growth, and the results suggest that 1,25 dihydroxy vitamin D3 may be an important factor in the regulation of cell growth.
the effect of the 1,25(OH)3 vitamin D3 on the epidermal receptor in BT-20 cells, which are known to have amplification of the EGF-R gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
1. 25(OH)D3 regulates the EGF-R level, but the mechanism is not clear.
1. 25(OH)D3 is a potent modulator of epidermal-growth-factor-receptor level and of epidermalgrowth factor internalization.
1. 25(OH) 2 D3 does not affect EGF internalization but it modifies the intracellular distribution of I-EGFR.

the 1.25-(OH)2D(3) is an inhibitor of EGF internalization and a regulator of EGG receptor level.
1.2.5 (OH)2 D3 regulates the EGF-R level and EGF internalization in BT-20 cells.
1.2.5 (OH)2-D3 is a regulator for the EGF receptor level in BT-2O cells, and it cannot be affirmed whether this effect occurs directly or is mediated by other parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of 1,25(OH) 2D3 on EGF binding and internalization in BT-20 cells was not mediated by an effect on the EGF-R level.
